questions.question_text: What is the best way to receive constructive criticism gracefully during a school project review or mock interview?

options.text: Interrupt the person giving feedback to explain why they’re wrong
Listen without interrupting, ask clarifying questions if needed, and thank them for their input
Ignore the feedback and focus only on what you think you did well
Get upset and walk away to avoid hearing more criticism

correct_answer.text: Listen without interrupting, ask clarifying questions if needed, and thank them for their input

questions.question_text: How can you turn rejection into motivation after not getting selected for a club or job?

options.text: Give up on trying for similar opportunities since you weren’t chosen
Feel disappointed for a short time, ask for feedback if possible, and use it as a learning opportunity to improve
Blame others for the decision and refuse to try again
Pretend the rejection didn’t happen and avoid thinking about it

correct_answer.text: Feel disappointed for a short time, ask for feedback if possible, and use it as a learning opportunity to improve

questions.question_text: Why is self-reflection important after a mock interview or class presentation?

options.text: It helps you criticize yourself harshly so you never make mistakes again
It allows you to identify what went well and what to improve, setting goals for next time
It’s only useful if someone else tells you what you did wrong
It wastes time since you can’t change what already happened

correct_answer.text: It allows you to identify what went well and what to improve, setting goals for next time

questions.question_text: What should you do if feedback from a teacher or coach feels unclear or confusing?

options.text: Assume they don’t know what they’re talking about and ignore it
Politely ask for clarification with a question like, “Can you explain what you mean by that?”
Argue with them to prove your point instead of listening
Nod and pretend you understand, even if you don’t

correct_answer.text: Politely ask for clarification with a question like, “Can you explain what you mean by that?”
